text:
alex: Heads-up — uploaded an nsys trace for the KV-cache refill tail on staging. timeline points to repeated H2D/D2H stalls and a bunch of peer-copy fallbacks to host path. trace: https://internal/trace/1785001234 :eyes:
perf-bot: nsys report ready — total stall time ~12.3s, ~68% correlated with kv cache refills (multiple small copies). See summary + kernel timeline in the trace.
priya: Which model/shape and batch sizes? is this on Dedicated or Hosted infra?
alex: Dedicated p4d-ish infra. Model is a medium decoder (seq=2048), bursts of concurrent requests ramping batch from 4 up to 16. The refill path kicks when kv-miss chain > 8 entries, we then do peer copies to pull KV shards.
mike: Quick skim — I saw long gaps labeled "MemcpyHtoD" and then a bunch of small kernel launches. Looks like some cudaPeerCopyAsync calls fell back to device-host-device. That would force pageable host traffic if pages aren't pinned.
hana: Do we have topo mismatch? nvlink peer mapping can cause fallback to staged host copy. run `nvidia-smi topo -m` on that node. Also check dmesg for IOMMU faults.
alex: I ran the topo — NVLink present between GPUs 0<->1 but not all pairs. The runtime chooses cudaMemcpyPeer when the CU can map; otherwise we call cuMemcpyAsync host-staged code path. The staged path uses our generic host buffer allocated with malloc (pageable). That matches the nsys hotspots.
priya: Oof. Pageable -> kernel-side page faults can be huge. Do we already have a pinned host buffer pool for KV copy staging?
alex: Not for this path, no. Current heuristic allocates a scratch host buffer on-demand and calls cuMemcpyAsync. On high concurrency this creates heavy page pinning pressure and stalls.
mike: Repro idea: microbench that exercises CuMemcpyPeerAsync vs cuMemcpyAsync(host) with pinned vs pageable and measure latency under contended load. I can sketch quickly. :+1:
hana: Short-term mitigation: pre-register a pool of pinned host buffers (cudaHostAlloc / cudaHostRegister) and prefer those for staged fallback. Also add a runtime flag to force peer-copy-only so we can fail fast for incompatible topologies.
alex: Agreed. Also kernel selection twist: when page-fault stalls occur the scheduler picks a different memcpy kernel (slower) — I saw a pattern where the runtime then switches batching heuristic to smaller batches because of increased per-token latency, which increases cache churn. Cascade effect.
priya: Could we change refill to coalesce small KV pulls into one larger peercopy to reduce number of host interactions?
mike: Yes — coalesce + pinned pool should help. Add a circuit: if peercopy fails for the target pair, try mapping via a per-epoch pinned staging buffer and do a single cuMemcpyAsync of the whole shard. Measure throughput.
perf-bot: Uploaded heavyweight trace + lightweight microbench profiles to the artifact store: s3://perf/traces/1785001234/{nsys-summary.json,memcpy-microbench.csv}
alan: (note: not participating)
alex: quick snippet of the pinned allocation I prototyped:
```
// allocate pinned pool
void* pool; cudaHostAlloc(&pool, POOL_SZ, cudaHostAllocPortable | cudaHostAllocMapped);
// use pool for staged copies: cudaMemcpyAsync(dstGpu, pool, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream);
```
priya: Nice. We should also add telemetry: counters for "peer-copy-fallback" and "pinned-alloc-fallback" so we can track frequency and latency impact.
hana: +1 on telemetry. Also add a check in rollout to log topo mismatches on node startup so Dedicated teams can tag nodes lacking full p2p.
mike: I'll create the microbench PR with numbers: expected ~10-20x faster for direct NVLink peercopy vs pageable host-staged under concurrency. Will post results here.
alex: Action items: 1) mike -> microbench + numbers (ETA today), 2) priya -> runtime flag + telemetry (ETA tomorrow), 3) hana -> ops check script for topo + node tags, 4) alex -> implement pinned pool prototype and run end-to-end traces.
priya: Sounds good. If pinned pool reduces stall time we'll test canary rollout. :rocket:
perf-bot: Reminder scheduled: perf-regression-checker will run nightly with the new microbench once PR is merged.
alex: Thanks — I'll post updated nsys timelines after the pinned-pool run.
mike: ping me when you need help with perf counters.
hana: i'll add the topo-check cron. :white_check_mark:
alex: closing loop — posted initial re-run (pinned pool) trace at https://internal/trace/1785001259 — early look shows stall time down from 12.3s -> 1.8s on same workload. More analysis incoming. :tada:
